 16  class FixedWidthSplitter(core.BaseSplitter):
 17      """
 18      Split line based on fixed start and end positions for each ``col`` in
 19      ``self.cols``.
 20
 21      This class requires that the Header class will have defined ``col.start``
 22      and ``col.end`` for each column.  The reference to the ``header.cols`` gets
 23      put in the splitter object by the base Reader.read() function just in time
 24      for splitting data lines by a ``data`` object.
 25
 26      Note that the ``start`` and ``end`` positions are defined in the pythonic
 27      style so line[start:end] is the desired substring for a column.  This splitter
 28      class does not have a hook for ``process_lines`` since that is generally not
 29      useful for fixed-width input.
 30
 31      """
 32
 33      delimiter_pad = ""
 34      bookend = False
 35      delimiter = "|"
 36
 37      def __call__(self, lines):
 38          for line in lines:
 39              vals = [line[x.start : x.end] for x in self.cols]
 40              if self.process_val:
 41                  yield [self.process_val(x) for x in vals]
 42              else:
 43                  yield vals
 44
 45      def join(self, vals, widths):
 46          pad = self.delimiter_pad or ""
 47          delimiter = self.delimiter or ""
 48          padded_delim = pad + delimiter + pad
 49          if self.bookend:
 50              bookend_left = delimiter + pad
 51              bookend_right = pad + delimiter
 52          else:
 53              bookend_left = ""
 54              bookend_right = ""
 55          vals = [" " * (width - len(val)) + val for val, width in zip(vals, widths)]
 56          return bookend_left + padded_delim.join(vals) + bookend_right
```

`FixedWidthHeader.splitter_class` for header-line splitting on `"|"`; RST overrides it
with `DefaultSplitter` in `SimpleRSTHeader`.)

## (5) How RST reads positions / `get_fixedwidth_params`

`FixedWidthHeader.get_fixedwidth_params` — fixedwidth.py:181-244:

```python
181    def get_fixedwidth_params(self, line):
182        """
183        Split ``line`` on the delimiter and determine column values and
184        column start and end positions.  This might include null columns with
185        zero length (e.g. for ``header row = "| col1 || col2 | col3 |"`` or
186        ``header2_row = "----- ------- -----"``).  The null columns are
187        stripped out.  Returns the values between delimiters and the
188        corresponding start and end positions.
189
190        Parameters
191        ----------
192        line : str
193            Input line
194
195        Returns
196        -------
197        vals : list
198            List of values.
199        starts : list
200            List of starting indices.
201        ends : list
202            List of ending indices.
203
204        """
205
206        # If column positions are already specified then just use those.
207        # If neither column starts or ends are given, figure out positions
208        # between delimiters. Otherwise, either the starts or the ends have
209        # been given, so figure out whichever wasn't given.
210        if self.col_starts is not None and self.col_ends is not None:
211            starts = list(self.col_starts)  # could be any iterable, e.g. np.array
212            # user supplies inclusive endpoint
213            ends = [x + 1 if x is not None else None for x in self.col_ends]
214            if len(starts) != len(ends):
215                raise ValueError(
216                    "Fixed width col_starts and col_ends must have the same length"
217                )
218            vals = [line[start:end].strip() for start, end in zip(starts, ends)]
219        elif self.col_starts is None and self.col_ends is None:
220            # There might be a cleaner way to do this but it works...
221            vals = line.split(self.splitter.delimiter)
222            starts = [0]
223            ends = []
224            for val in vals:
225                if val:
226                    ends.append(starts[-1] + len(val))
227                    starts.append(ends[-1] + 1)
228                else:
229                    starts[-1] += 1
230            starts = starts[:-1]
231            vals = [x.strip() for x in vals if x]
232            if len(vals) != len(starts) or len(vals) != len(ends):
233                raise InconsistentTableError("Error parsing fixed width header")
234        else:
235            # exactly one of col_starts or col_ends is given...
236            if self.col_starts is not None:
237                starts = list(self.col_starts)
238                ends = starts[1:] + [None]  # Assume each col ends where the next starts
239            else:  # self.col_ends is not None
240                ends = [x + 1 for x in self.col_ends]
241                starts = [0] + ends[:-1]  # Assume each col starts where the last ended
242            vals = [line[start:end].strip() for start, end in zip(starts, ends)]
243
244        return vals, starts, ends

### Read-path walkthrough (how positions are derived for an RST read)

For a table like the ones in test_rst.py (blank line + comment above; line indices after
`process_lines` which strips comments/blank lines via Basic.process_lines — the table rows
seen by `get_cols` are the 4-line `====` / header / `====` / data... block; note
`SimpleRSTData.start_line = 3` skips to data at row index 3, i.e. first data row comes
after the second `====` line and the trailing `====` is dropped by `end_line = -1`):

1. `SimpleRSTHeader.get_cols` (inherited, fixedwidth.py:84) runs with `start_line = 1`,
   `position_line = 0` (rst.py:17-18), `header_rows = ["name"]` (default from
   `FixedWidth.__init__`, fixedwidth.py:345-357 — RST passes no `header_rows`).
2. `position_line` branch (fixedwidth.py:135-160): `get_line(lines, 0)` = first `====`
   line; charset check passes (`=` is in `set_of_position_line_characters`,
   fixedwidth.py:74); `get_fixedwidth_params(line)` with `col_starts`/`col_ends` both
   None splits on `self.splitter.delimiter` — for RST that is `DefaultSplitter`
   (whitespace, since `splitter_class = DefaultSplitter`, rst.py:19), so the `====`
   groups give col_starts/col_ends of each `=` run; stored on the header as
   `self.col_starts` / `self.col_ends`.
3. Then fixedwidth.py:163-164: `get_line(lines, start_line)` = header name line;

class FixedWidthSplitter(core.BaseSplitter):
    """
    Split line based on fixed start and end positions for each ``col`` in
    ``self.cols``.

    This class requires that the Header class will have defined ``col.start``
    and ``col.end`` for each column.  The reference to the ``header.cols`` gets
    put in the splitter object by the base Reader.read() function just in time
    for splitting data lines by a ``data`` object.

    class does not have a hook for ``process_lines`` since that is generally not
    useful for fixed-width input.

    """

    delimiter_pad = ""
    bookend = False
    delimiter = "|"

    def __call__(self, lines):
        for line in lines:
            vals = [line[x.start : x.end] for x in self.cols]
            if self.process_val:
                yield [self.process_val(x) for x in vals]
            else:
                yield vals

    def join(self, vals, widths):
        pad = self.delimiter_pad or ""
        delimiter = self.delimiter or ""

        if self.bookend:
            bookend_left = delimiter + pad
            bookend_right = pad + delimiter
        else:

            bookend_right = ""

 17      """
 18      Split line based on fixed start and end positions for each ``col`` in
 19      ``self.cols``.
 20
 21      This class requires that the Header class will have defined ``col.start``
 22      and ``col.end`` for each column.  The reference to the ``header.cols`` gets
 23      put in the splitter object by the base Reader.read() function just in time
 24      for splitting data lines by a ``data`` object.
 25
 26      Note that the ``start`` and ``end`` positions are defined in the pythonic
 27      style so line[start:end] is the desired substring for a column.  This splitter
 28      class does not have a hook for ``process_lines`` since that is generally not
 29      useful for fixed-width input.
 30
 31      """
 32

 34      bookend = False
 35      delimiter = "|"
 36
 37      def __call__(self, lines):
 38          for line in lines:
 39              vals = [line[x.start : x.end] for x in self.cols]
 40              if self.process_val:
 41                  yield [self.process_val(x) for x in vals]
 42              else:
 43                  yield vals
 44
 45      def join(self, vals, widths):
 46          pad = self.delimiter_pad or ""
 47          delimiter = self.delimiter or ""
 48          padded_delim = pad + delimiter + pad
 49          if self.bookend:
 50              bookend_left = delimiter + pad
 51              bookend_right = pad + delimiter
 52          else:
 53              bookend_left = ""
 54              bookend_right = ""
 55          vals = [" " * (width - len(val)) + val for val, width in zip(vals, widths)]
 56          return bookend_left + padded_delim.join(vals) + bookend_right

182        """
183        Split ``line`` on the delimiter and determine column values and
184        column start and end positions.  This might include null columns with
185        zero length (e.g. for ``header row = "| col1 || col2 | col3 |"`` or
186        ``header2_row = "----- ------- -----"``).  The null columns are
187        stripped out.  Returns the values between delimiters and the
188        corresponding start and end positions.
189
190        Parameters
191        ----------
192        line : str
193            Input line
194
195        Returns
196        -------
197        vals : list
198            List of values.
199        starts : list
200            List of starting indices.
201        ends : list
202            List of ending indices.
203
204        """
205
206        # If column positions are already specified then just use those.
207        # If neither column starts or ends are given, figure out positions
208        # between delimiters. Otherwise, either the starts or the ends have
209        # been given, so figure out whichever wasn't given.
210        if self.col_starts is not None and self.col_ends is not None:
211            starts = list(self.col_starts)  # could be any iterable, e.g. np.array
212            # user supplies inclusive endpoint
213            ends = [x + 1 if x is not None else None for x in self.col_ends]
214            if len(starts) != len(ends):
215                raise ValueError(
216                    "Fixed width col_starts and col_ends must have the same length"
217                )
218            vals = [line[start:end].strip() for start, end in zip(starts, ends)]
219        elif self.col_starts is None and self.col_ends is None:
220            # There might be a cleaner way to do this but it works...
221            vals = line.split(self.splitter.delimiter)
222            starts = [0]
223            ends = []
224            for val in vals:
225                if val:
226                    ends.append(starts[-1] + len(val))
227                    starts.append(ends[-1] + 1)
228                else:
229                    starts[-1] += 1
230            starts = starts[:-1]
231            vals = [x.strip() for x in vals if x]
232            if len(vals) != len(starts) or len(vals) != len(ends):
233                raise InconsistentTableError("Error parsing fixed width header")
234        else:
235            # exactly one of col_starts or col_ends is given...
236            if self.col_starts is not None:
237                starts = list(self.col_starts)
238                ends = starts[1:] + [None]  # Assume each col ends where the next starts
239            else:  # self.col_ends is not None
240                ends = [x + 1 for x in self.col_ends]
241                starts = [0] + ends[:-1]  # Assume each col starts where the last ended
242            vals = [line[start:end].strip() for start, end in zip(starts, ends)]

 16  class FixedWidthSplitter(core.BaseSplitter):
 17      """
 18      Split line based on fixed start and end positions for each ``col`` in
 19      ``self.cols``.
 20
 21      This class requires that the Header class will have defined ``col.start``
 22      and ``col.end`` for each column.  The reference to the ``header.cols`` gets
 23      put in the splitter object by the base Reader.read() function just in time
 24      for splitting data lines by a ``data`` object.
 25
 26      Note that the ``start`` and ``end`` positions are defined in the pythonic
 27      style so line[start:end] is the desired substring for a column.  This splitter
 28      class does not have a hook for ``process_lines`` since that is generally not
 29      useful for fixed-width input.
 30
 31      """
 32
 33      delimiter_pad = ""
 34      bookend = False
 35      delimiter = "|"
 36
 37      def __call__(self, lines):
 38          for line in lines:
 39              vals = [line[x.start : x.end] for x in self.cols]
 40              if self.process_val:
 41                  yield [self.process_val(x) for x in vals]
 42              else:
 43                  yield vals
 44
 45      def join(self, vals, widths):
 46          pad = self.delimiter_pad or ""
 47          delimiter = self.delimiter or ""
 48          padded_delim = pad + delimiter + pad
 49          if self.bookend:
 50              bookend_left = delimiter + pad
 51              bookend_right = pad + delimiter
 52          else:
 53              bookend_left = ""
 54              bookend_right = ""
 55          vals = [" " * (width - len(val)) + val for val, width in zip(vals, widths)]
 56          return bookend_left + padded_delim.join(vals) + bookend_right

208        # between delimiters. Otherwise, either the starts or the ends have
209        # been given, so figure out whichever wasn't given.
210        if self.col_starts is not None and self.col_ends is not None:

223            ends = []

227                    starts.append(ends[-1] + 1)
228                else:

 17      """
 18      Split line based on fixed start and end positions for each ``col`` in
 19      ``self.cols``.
 20
 21      This class requires that the Header class will have defined ``col.start``
 22      and ``col.end`` for each column.  The reference to the ``header.cols`` gets

 24      for splitting data lines by a ``data`` object.
 25

 27      style so line[start:end] is the desired substring for a column.  This splitter
 28      class does not have a hook for ``process_lines`` since that is generally not
 29      useful for fixed-width input.
 30

 34      bookend = False
 35      delimiter = "|"

 40              if self.process_val:

183        Split ``line`` on the delimiter and determine column values and
184        column start and end positions.  This might include null columns with
185        zero length (e.g. for ``header row = "| col1 || col2 | col3 |"`` or
186        ``header2_row = "----- ------- -----"``).  The null columns are
187        stripped out.  Returns the values between delimiters and the
188        corresponding start and end positions.
189
190        Parameters
191        ----------
192        line : str
193            Input line
194
195        Returns
196        -------
197        vals : list
198            List of values.
199        starts : list
200            List of starting indices.
201        ends : list
202            List of ending indices.
203
204        """
205
206        # If column positions are already specified then just use those.
207        # If neither column starts or ends are given, figure out positions
208        # between delimiters. Otherwise, either the starts or the ends have
209        # been given, so figure out whichever wasn't given.
210        if self.col_starts is not None and self.col_ends is not None:
211            starts = list(self.col_starts)  # could be any iterable, e.g. np.array
212            # user supplies inclusive endpoint
213            ends = [x + 1 if x is not None else None for x in self.col_ends]
214            if len(starts) != len(ends):
215                raise ValueError(
216                    "Fixed width col_starts and col_ends must have the same length"
217                )
218            vals = [line[start:end].strip() for start, end in zip(starts, ends)]
219        elif self.col_starts is None and self.col_ends is None:
220            # There might be a cleaner way to do this but it works...
221            vals = line.split(self.splitter.delimiter)
222            starts = [0]
223            ends = []
224            for val in vals:
225                if val:
226                    ends.append(starts[-1] + len(val))
227                    starts.append(ends[-1] + 1)
228                else:
229                    starts[-1] += 1
230            starts = starts[:-1]
231            vals = [x.strip() for x in vals if x]
232            if len(vals) != len(starts) or len(vals) != len(ends):
233                raise InconsistentTableError("Error parsing fixed width header")
234        else:
235            # exactly one of col_starts or col_ends is given...
236            if self.col_starts is not None:
237                starts = list(self.col_starts)
238                ends = starts[1:] + [None]  # Assume each col ends where the next starts
239            else:  # self.col_ends is not None
240                ends = [x + 1 for x in self.col_ends]
241                starts = [0] + ends[:-1]  # Assume each col starts where the last ended

 27      style so line[start:end] is the desired substring for a column.  This splitter
 28      class does not have a hook for ``process_lines`` since that is generally not
 29      useful for fixed-width input.
 30
 31      """
 32
 33      delimiter_pad = ""
 34      bookend = False
 35      delimiter = "|"
 36
 37      def __call__(self, lines):
 38          for line in lines:
 39              vals = [line[x.start : x.end] for x in self.cols]
 40              if self.process_val:
 41                  yield [self.process_val(x) for x in vals]
 42              else:
 43                  yield vals
 44
 45      def join(self, vals, widths):
 46          pad = self.delimiter_pad or ""
 47          delimiter = self.delimiter or ""
 48          padded_delim = pad + delimiter + pad
 49          if self.bookend:
 50              bookend_left = delimiter + pad
 51              bookend_right = pad + delimiter
 52          else:
 53              bookend_left = ""
 54              bookend_right = ""
 55          vals = [" " * (width - len(val)) + val for val, width in zip(vals, widths)]
 56          return bookend_left + padded_delim.join(vals) + bookend_right
```

`FixedWidthHeader.splitter_class` for header-line splitting on `"|"`; RST overrides it

`FixedWidthHeader.get_fixedwidth_params` — fixedwidth.py:181-244:

```python
181    def get_fixedwidth_params(self, line):
182        """
183        Split ``line`` on the delimiter and determine column values and
184        column start and end positions.  This might include null columns with
185        zero length (e.g. for ``header row = "| col1 || col2 | col3 |"`` or
186        ``header2_row = "----- ------- -----"``).  The null columns are
187        stripped out.  Returns the values between delimiters and the
188        corresponding start and end positions.
189
190        Parameters
191        ----------
192        line : str
193            Input line
194
195        Returns
196        -------
197        vals : list
198            List of values.
199        starts : list
200            List of starting indices.
201        ends : list
202            List of ending indices.
203
204        """
205
206        # If column positions are already specified then just use those.
207        # If neither column starts or ends are given, figure out positions
208        # between delimiters. Otherwise, either the starts or the ends have
209        # been given, so figure out whichever wasn't given.
210        if self.col_starts is not None and self.col_ends is not None:
211            starts = list(self.col_starts)  # could be any iterable, e.g. np.array
212            # user supplies inclusive endpoint
213            ends = [x + 1 if x is not None else None for x in self.col_ends]
214            if len(starts) != len(ends):
215                raise ValueError(
216                    "Fixed width col_starts and col_ends must have the same length"
217                )
218            vals = [line[start:end].strip() for start, end in zip(starts, ends)]
219        elif self.col_starts is None and self.col_ends is None:
220            # There might be a cleaner way to do this but it works...
221            vals = line.split(self.splitter.delimiter)
222            starts = [0]
223            ends = []
224            for val in vals:
225                if val:
226                    ends.append(starts[-1] + len(val))
227                    starts.append(ends[-1] + 1)
228                else:
229                    starts[-1] += 1
230            starts = starts[:-1]
231            vals = [x.strip() for x in vals if x]
232            if len(vals) != len(starts) or len(vals) != len(ends):
233                raise InconsistentTableError("Error parsing fixed width header")
234        else:
235            # exactly one of col_starts or col_ends is given...
236            if self.col_starts is not None:
237                starts = list(self.col_starts)
238                ends = starts[1:] + [None]  # Assume each col ends where the next starts
239            else:  # self.col_ends is not None
240                ends = [x + 1 for x in self.col_ends]
241                starts = [0] + ends[:-1]  # Assume each col starts where the last ended
242            vals = [line[start:end].strip() for start, end in zip(starts, ends)]
243
244        return vals, starts, ends

### Read-path walkthrough (how positions are derived for an RST read)

For a table like the ones in test_rst.py (blank line + comment above; line indices after
`process_lines` which strips comments/blank lines via Basic.process_lines — the table rows
seen by `get_cols` are the 4-line `====` / header / `====` / data... block; note
`SimpleRSTData.start_line = 3` skips to data at row index 3, i.e. first data row comes
after the second `====` line and the trailing `====` is dropped by `end_line = -1`):

1. `SimpleRSTHeader.get_cols` (inherited, fixedwidth.py:84) runs with `start_line = 1`,
   `position_line = 0` (rst.py:17-18), `header_rows = ["name"]` (default from
   `FixedWidth.__init__`, fixedwidth.py:345-357 — RST passes no `header_rows`).
2. `position_line` branch (fixedwidth.py:135-160): `get_line(lines, 0)` = first `====`
   line; charset check passes (`=` is in `set_of_position_line_characters`,
   fixedwidth.py:74); `get_fixedwidth_params(line)` with `col_starts`/`col_ends` both
   None splits on `self.splitter.delimiter` — for RST that is `DefaultSplitter`
   (whitespace, since `splitter_class = DefaultSplitter`, rst.py:19), so the `====`
   groups give col_starts/col_ends of each `=` run; stored on the header as
   `self.col_starts` / `self.col_ends`.
3. Then fixedwidth.py:163-164: `get_line(lines, start_line)` = header name line;
   `get_fixedwidth_params(line)` again — but now `col_starts`/`col_ends` are set, so it
   takes the first branch (fixedwidth.py:210-218) slicing the name line at those
   positions. `SimpleRSTHeader.get_fixedwidth_params` (rst.py:22-26) then sets
   `ends[-1] = None` (unbounded last column).
4. `col.start`/`col.end` set at fixedwidth.py:177-179; data rows are sliced by
   `FixedWidthSplitter.__call__` (fixedwidth.py:37-43) via
   `FixedWidthTwoLineDataSplitter` (only difference: `delimiter = " "`).

### Implications for a write-only fix

- RST *write* path is `RST.write` (rst.py:63-66) -> `FixedWidth.write` (not shown, it
  delegates to `FixedWidthData.write`, fixedwidth.py:261-311). `FixedWidthData.write`
  emits: (a) header-name row(s), (b) a position line of `position_char` ("=") runs when
  `self.header.position_line is not None` (fixedwidth.py:296-299), (c) data rows — all
  via `FixedWidthSplitter.join` (fixedwidth.py:45-56) with `delimiter_pad=None`,
  `bookend=False`. Then `RST.write` duplicates `lines[1]` (the `====` position line) as
  the last line.
- None of the read-side symbols (`SimpleRSTHeader`, `SimpleRSTData`,
  `FixedWidthHeader.get_cols/get_line/get_fixedwidth_params`) are touched by
  `RST.write` or `FixedWidthData.write`. So a change confined to the write path
  (`RST.write` / `FixedWidthData.write` / `FixedWidthSplitter.join`) does not alter the
  read path.
- The only test that constrains write output is `test_write_normal`
  (test_rst.py:173-187), which asserts exact 6-line output:
  `==== ========= ==== ====` / `Col1      Col2 Col3 Col4` / same `====` line /
  two data rows / same `====` line. Any write-path change must keep `lines[1]` (the
  position line) as the `====`-runs row and the column layout produced by
  `FixedWidthSplitter.join` (fixedwidth.py:45-56): with `delimiter_pad=None`, `pad=""`,
  `bookend=False`, so the inter-column separator is three spaces (`padded_delim = " " +
  " " + " "`) and every value (header, position, data) is right-justified to its column
  width via `" " * (width - len(val)) + val`. The expected string in test_rst.py:180-185
  encodes exactly this.
- All 7 other tests in test_rst.py are pure read tests (`ascii.read`/
  `get_reader(...).read`) and are unaffected by any write-only change as long as the
